report_name: Hackers Trojanize TrueConf Installers with PhantomCore Backdoor

threat_actors.name: Head Mare
threat_actors.description: A hacktivist group conducting a supply chain attack campaign targeting unpatched TrueConf video conferencing servers. They exploit vulnerabilities to gain system-level privileges, deploy web shells, and replace legitimate client installers with trojanized versions containing the PhantomCore and PhantomGraph backdoors.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Attackers exploited two vulnerabilities (KLCERT-26-057 and KLCERT-26-058) in the internet-facing TrueConf server to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: Attackers exploited a vulnerability (KLCERT-26-058) to escape the application sandbox and escalate privileges to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on the compromised TrueConf server.

attack_patterns.name: Web Shell
attack_patterns.description: A web shell was deployed on the compromised TrueConf server to provide persistent remote access and facilitate the replacement of the client installer.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: Attackers replaced the legitimate TrueConf client installer on the compromised server with a trojanized version, turning the server into a malware distribution point for end users.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
attack_patterns.description: The PhantomGraph backdoor is capable of dumping credentials from the LSASS process on compromised systems.

attack_patterns.name: Web Service
attack_patterns.description: The PhantomGraph backdoor used Microsoft OneDrive, a legitimate public web service, for command and control to evade network detection.

attack_patterns.name: Proxy: External Proxy
attack_patterns.description: The PhantomGraph backdoor has the capability to create reverse SSH tunnels, creating an external proxy into the compromised network for long-term access.

malware.name: PhantomCore
malware.description: The primary backdoor delivered via the trojanized TrueConf client installer. It provides the initial foothold on client machines.

malware.name: PhantomGraph
malware.description: An advanced backdoor consisting of two DLLs that uses Microsoft OneDrive for C2, dumps LSASS credentials, and can create reverse SSH tunnels.

tools.name: TrueConf Client
tools.description: The legitimate TrueConf video conferencing client installer, which was replaced with a trojanized version on compromised servers to deliver the PhantomCore backdoor.

tools.name: SSH
tools.description: Used by the PhantomGraph backdoor to create reverse tunnels, providing a proxy into the compromised network.

vulnerabilities.name: KLCERT-26-057
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in TrueConf servers that allows for malicious script execution within the application's isolated environment. It was the first part of an exploit chain used by Head Mare.

vulnerabilities.name: KLCERT-26-058
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in TrueConf servers that allows an attacker to escape the application's sandbox and execute commands on the underlying Windows OS. It was used for privilege escalation to SYSTEM.

identities.name: TrueConf
identities.description: The vendor of the video conferencing server software that was targeted by the Head Mare group. The attackers exploited vulnerabilities in the server and trojanized the client installers distributed by it.

identities.name: Russian organizations
identities.description: Organizations in Russia across critical sectors (electronics, transportation, energy, government) that use unpatched TrueConf servers and were targeted by the Head Mare group.

infrastructure.name: Web Shell on TrueConf Server
infrastructure.description: A web shell deployed on compromised TrueConf servers to maintain persistent access and replace the legitimate client installer.

infrastructure.name: PhantomGraph OneDrive C2
infrastructure.description: A Microsoft OneDrive account used as a command and control channel by the PhantomGraph backdoor.

indicators.name: Suspicious Outbound Connection to OneDrive from Server
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Outbound Connection to OneDrive from Server
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4f7a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: Detects network connections from common server processes to Microsoft OneDrive, which may indicate the use of OneDrive for C2 by malware like PhantomGraph.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-breach-trueconf-to-trojanize-client-installers-with-backdoors/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-08
tags:
  - attack.t1102
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Initiated: true
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - 'onedrive.live.com'
      - '1drv.com'
  filter_server_procs:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '\tomcat.exe'
      - '\TrueConf-Server.exe'
  condition: selection and filter_server_procs
indicators.description: Detects network connections from server processes to Microsoft OneDrive. The article notes that the PhantomGraph backdoor uses OneDrive for C2, and such traffic from a server is anomalous.

indicators.name: Reverse SSH Tunnel Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: Reverse SSH Tunnel Creation
id: a2b3c4d5-e6f7-4a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a reverse SSH tunnel using the 'ssh -R' command, a technique used by malware like PhantomGraph to establish a persistent backdoor into a network.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-breach-trueconf-to-trojanize-client-installers-with-backdoors/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-08
tags:
  - attack.t1090.002
  - attack.command_and_control
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\ssh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: ' -R '
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of a reverse SSH tunnel, a technique explicitly mentioned as a capability of the PhantomGraph backdoor.

indicators.name: Suspicious Child Process of TrueConf Web Server
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Child Process of TrueConf Web Server
id: b3c4d5e6-f7a8-4b9c-0d1e-2f3a4b5c6d7e
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious child processes (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawned by the TrueConf web server process (e.g., w3wp.exe), which could indicate web shell execution.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-breach-trueconf-to-trojanize-client-installers-with-backdoors/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-08
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects suspicious child processes spawned by a web server process, which is a common indicator of web shell activity as described in the attack chain.
